title: Permutations and Combinations: Counting Without Listing

questions.question: In how many ways can 3 books be arranged on a shelf, chosen from 5 different books?
questions.rationale: Order matters on a shelf, so use permutations: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60. Choosing without arranging would give the combination 10.

questions.question: What is 0! (zero factorial)?
questions.rationale: There is exactly one way to arrange nothing, so 0! = 1 by definition. This convention also keeps n!/(n−r)! correct when r = 0 or r = n.

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements can be made from the letters of MISSISSIPPI?
questions.rationale: 11 letters with I repeated 4 times, S 4 times, P twice: 11!/(4! × 4! × 2!) = 39916800/1152 = 34650. Identical letters must be divided out.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 people be seated around a round table?
questions.rationale: Rotations are the same seating, so fix one person and permute the other 4: (5 − 1)! = 24. The linear answer 120 counts each ring 5 times over.

questions.question: How many committees of 3 people can be formed from 8 people?
questions.rationale: A committee has no order, so use combinations: C(8,3) = 8 × 7 × 6 / 3! = 336/6 = 56. The permutation 336 counts every committee 3! times over.

questions.question: How many handshakes occur when 10 people each shake hands once with everyone else?
questions.rationale: A handshake is an unordered pair: C(10,2) = 45. Multiplying 10 × 9 = 90 double-counts, since A shaking B's hand is the same event as B shaking A's.

questions.question: In how many ways can 7 identical sweets be distributed among 3 children?
questions.rationale: Stars and bars: place 2 dividers among 9 slots (7 sweets + 2 dividers): C(9,2) = 36. The formula is C(n + r − 1, r − 1) for n identical items and r receivers.

questions.question: Which relation between permutations and combinations is correct?
questions.rationale: Each unordered selection of r items can be ordered r! ways, so permutations = combinations × r!. Dividing instead of multiplying reverses the logic.

questions.question: How many 4-letter codes can be made from A, B, C, D using each letter exactly once?
questions.rationale: All 4 letters are used in order: 4! = 24. Codes like ABCD and DCAB are different because order matters.

questions.question: What is the fastest way to evaluate C(10, 8)?
questions.rationale: Symmetry C(n, r) = C(n, n − r) turns C(10, 8) into C(10, 2) = 45 — choosing who is out is as good as choosing who is in.
